sections.english: All that you pray to reach at some point in the circuit of your life can be yours now — if you are generous to yourself. That is, if you leave all the past behind, entrust the future to Providence, and direct the present solely to reverence and justice. To reverence, so that you come to love your given lot: nature brought it to you and you to it. To justice, so that you speak the truth freely and without complication, and act only as law and the individual value of things dictates.
sections.chinese: 凡你所求于生命轮回中某一天才达成的，此刻便可归你所有——若你愿厚待你自己。那即是：若你放下所有过去，将未来托付于天意，而将当下专致于虔敬与正义。虔敬，使你终能爱你所被分派之命运：自然将它带给你，也将你带给它。正义，使你从容而无迂曲地言说真理，仅依法则及事物本身之固有价值行事。

sections.english: If, then, when you finally come close to your exit, you have left all else behind and value only your directing mind and the divinity within you, if your fear is not that you will cease to live, but that you never started a life in accordance with nature, then you will be a man worthy of the universe that gave you birth.
sections.chinese: 若你最终临近辞世之时，已将一切他物释去，唯珍视你主导之心智与内里之神性；若你所忧惧者不是你之生命将终，而是你从未曾开启过依自然而活的一生——那么，你将是一个堪配那诞你出世的宇宙之人。

sections.english: God sees all our directing minds stripped of their material vessels, their husks and their dross. His contact is only between his own intelligence and what has flowed from him into these channels of ours. If you train yourself to do the same, you will be rid of what so much distracts you.
sections.chinese: 神观照吾辈所有主导之心智时，是将其物质之容器、外壳与渣滓皆剥离净尽的。他的接触，仅在他自己的智识与那自他流出而入于我等此诸通道者之间。你若训练自己做同样的事，便将摆脱那如此纷扰你心之物。

sections.english: I have often wondered how it is that everyone loves himself more than anyone else, but rates his own judgement of himself below that of others. Anyway, if a god or some wise tutor appeared at his side and told him to entertain no internal thought or intention which he won't immediately broadcast out loud, he would not stand it for a single day. So it is that we respect what our neighbours will think of us more than what we think of ourselves.
sections.chinese: 我常感到疑虑：人皆自爱胜于爱他人，却把自己对己之评价置于他人评价之下。无论如何，若有神或某位明师现于彼之身旁，令他不得在心中存有任何一经丝毫思考便不能立即琅琅宣之于口的内在之思与意想，那他连一天也无法忍受。由此看来，我们之重邻人对己之想，胜于重自己内心之所思。

sections.english: Practise even what you have despaired of mastering. For lack of practice the left hand is awkward for most tasks, but has a stronger grip on the bridle than the right — it is practised in this.
sections.chinese: 即便是你已绝望而放弃精熟之事，仍当予以练习。因欠缺练习，左手在多数任务中略显笨拙，然其握缰时的劲道却强过右手——正因为它在此一点上经了锻炼。

sections.english: How one should be in both body and soul when overtaken by death; the shortness of life; the immensity of time future and past; the feebleness of all things material.
sections.chinese: 当死亡降临时，人之身与心当处于何等状态；生命何其短促；过去与未来时间之浩瀚无穷；一切物质事物之脆弱不堪。

sections.english: Look at causation stripped bare of its covers; look at the ulterior reference of any action. Consider, what is pain? What is pleasure? What is death? What is fame? Who is not himself the cause of his own unrest? Reflect how no one is hampered by any other; and that all is as thinking makes it so.
sections.chinese: 观照那被剥去了外罩、赤裸裸的原因；观照任何行动背后之援引指向。思量：痛苦为何物？逸乐为何物？死为何物？名声为何物？谁不是自己内心不宁之原因？反思何以无人能被他人所桎梏；以及一切皆如思之所成。

sections.english: The model for the application of your principles is the boxer rather than the gladiator. The gladiator puts down or takes up the sword he uses, but the boxer always has his hands and needs only to clench them into fists.
sections.chinese: 运用你之诸原则时，其模范当为拳手而非剑斗士。剑斗士将其所用之剑或放下或拾起，然拳手之双手常在其身，只须握而为拳即可。

sections.english: See things for what they are, analysing into material, cause, and reference.
sections.chinese: 观事物如其本然，将其分析成物质、原因与指向。

sections.english: What liberty man has to do only what god will approve, and to welcome all that god assigns him in the course of nature!
sections.chinese: 人拥有何等之自由——唯行神所肯定之事，并欢迎神于自然之行程中所分配于他的一切！

sections.english: Do not blame the gods: they do no wrong, willed or unwilled. Do not blame men either: all their wrongs are unwilled. No one, then, should be blamed.
sections.chinese: 莫归责于诸神：他们不行错事，无论是有意或无意。也莫归责于人：他们所有的过失皆非其本意。如此，便无人当被归责。

sections.english: How absurd — and a complete stranger to the world — is the man surprised at any aspect of his experience in life!
sections.chinese: 对其生命经验之任何层面感到意外的那人，何其荒谬——且全然是此世之一陌客！

sections.english: Either the compulsion of destiny and an order allowing no deviation, or a providence open to prayer, or a random welter without direction. Now if undeviating compulsion, why resist it? If a providence admitting the placation of prayer, make yourself worthy of divine assistance. If an ungoverned welter, be glad that in such a maelstrom you have within yourself a directing mind of your own.
sections.chinese: 要么是命运之必然与一无以偏离的秩序，要么是一开放于祈祷的天意，要么是漫无方向之随机混沌。若是不移不易之必然，何故抗拒？若是容许祈祷告慰之天意，便令己配得上神灵之佑助。若是一无主之混沌，你当欣幸，于此漩涡之中你自身内里尚有自己的一个主导心灵。

sections.english: The light of a lamp shines on and does not lose its radiance until it is extinguished. Will then the truth, justice, and self-control which fuel you fail before your own end?
sections.chinese: 灯之光芒持续照耀，直至熄灭方失去其辉华。那么，那些燃亮你生命的真理、正义与自制，难道会先于你自身之终点而消陨吗？

sections.english: If it is not right, don't do it: if it is not true, don't say it.
sections.chinese: 若非正确的，便不要去做；若非真实的，便不要去说。

sections.english: Your impulse on every occasion should be to a complete survey of what exactly this thing is which is making an impression on your mind — to open it out by analysis into cause, material, reference, and the time-span within which it must cease to be.
sections.chinese: 你的冲动在每一情形下，皆应导向一番彻底之勘察：究竟是何物在你心中留下了此一印象——将其以分析之法展开为原因、物质、指向，以及其必定终了之时间限度。

sections.english: Realize at long last that you have within you something stronger and more numinous than those agents of emotion which make you a mere puppet on their strings. What is in my mind at this very moment? Fear, is it? Suspicion? Desire? Something else of that sort?
sections.chinese: 你终须了悟：你内在有着比那些将你当作提线木偶之情绪作用者更加强大、更有神性分量之某物。此刻我心中在思何所想？恐惧乎？猜忌乎？贪欲乎？抑或某种别般类此之物？

sections.english: First, nothing aimless or without ulterior reference. Second, no reference to any end other than the common good.
sections.chinese: 其一，凡事不可漫无目的或全无遥远之依指。其二，不可指向任何不同于共同福祉之目的。

sections.english: That in a short while you will be nobody and nowhere; and the same of all that you now see and all who are now alive. It is the nature of all things to change, to perish and be transformed, so that in succession different things can come to be.
sections.chinese: 稍过片刻，你便将寂寂无名、无处可觅；而你此刻所见一切、此刻一切在世之人，亦莫不皆然。变化、消亡、转化——此乃一切事物之本然，以使继之而起的不同之物得以生现。

sections.english: That all is as thinking makes it so — and you control your thinking. So remove your judgements whenever you wish and then there is calm — as the sailor rounding the cape finds smooth water and the welcome of a waveless bay.
sections.chinese: 一切皆如思之所成——而你掌控着你的思。那么，随时随地，移除你的判断，随后便是风平浪静——正如水手绕过了岬角，便迎来平滑如镜之水波与那无浪湾澳之拥抱。

sections.english: Three thoughts to keep at hand. First: in your own actions, nothing aimless or other than Justice herself would have done; in external happenings either chance or providence is at work, and one should not blame chance or indict providence. Second: the nature of each of us from conception to the first breath, and from that point to the giving up of the ghost. Third: you could be caught up to the sky at any moment, then think what sort of people you would leave, and the life they would then lead.
sections.chinese: 三桩须臾莫忘之念。其一：于己之行动，无一漫无目的或非正义本身所会做之事；于外在之变故，或机遇或天意所运，人不应责难机遇或指控天意。其二：吾辈每人之本性——自存孕之始成至始有呼吸那一刻，再自此而至气息归断之时刻。其三：你任一顷刻间可能便被提升触天而去，然后，不妨想想你将丢下的是些什么样的人，以及他们随后将过着何种生命。

sections.english: Jettison the judgement, and you are saved. And who is there to prevent this jettison?
sections.chinese: 抛掉那判断，你便得救了。那么，又有谁能阻止你将其抛掉？

sections.english: When you fret at any circumstance, you have forgotten a number of things. You have forgotten that all comes about in accordance with the nature of the Whole; that any wrong done lies with the other; further, that everything which happens was always so in the past, will be the same again in the future, and is now happening everywhere in the present. You have also forgotten the close kinship of each individual to the whole human race.
sections.chinese: 每当你为一处境而烦恼不宁，你已忘了若干事。你忘了：一切都依循宇宙整体之本性而发生；你忘了：任何所行之错皆留在那人自己那里；再者，你忘了：一切所发生之事昔日向来如此，将来亦将同样复现，而此刻在一切所在之处正亦发生着同样之事。你还忘了：每一个体与全人类之间那种密迩的、血缘般的亲近连带。

sections.english: Continually review in your mind those whom a particular anger took to extremes, those who reached the greatest heights of glory or disaster or enmity or any other sort of fortune. Then stop and think: where is it all now? Smoke and ashes, a story told or even a story forgotten.
sections.chinese: 持之不断地在心间回溯：那些曾为一腔特殊之怒引入极端的人，那些曾蹿升到荣耀、或灾难、或仇怨、或任何其他命运之顶峰的人。而后，驻足凝想：这一切如今安在？烟云、与灰烬——一桩被人传叙的故事，或甚至一则早已为人遗忘的往事。

sections.english: To those who ask, 'Where then have you seen the gods? What conviction of their existence leads you to this worship of them?', I reply first that they are in fact visible to our eyes. Secondly, and notwithstanding, that I have not seen my own soul either, and yet I honour it. So it is with the gods too: from my repeated experience of their power I am convinced that they exist and I revere them.
sections.chinese: 对那些问道「那么你在哪里见过诸神？你对他们存在之确信因何而起，竟至使你如此敬拜他们？」的人，我首先回答说：他们事实上是可见于吾辈的双目的。其次——即使撇开此点——我亦未曾见识过我自己的灵魂，然我却尊崇它。诸神亦复如此：从我反复体验其大能的经验中，我深信他们存在，并虔敬他们。

sections.english: The salvation of life lies in seeing each object in its essence and its entirety, discerning both the material and the causal: in applying one's whole soul to doing right and speaking the truth. There remains only the enjoyment of living a linked succession of good deeds, with not the slightest gap between them.
sections.chinese: 生命之救赎，在于照见每一对象之本质与整全，辨别物质与原因二者：在于以整个灵魂投入于行义举、说真话之中。此外所余者，仅是乐享于一连串环环相接的善行交织而成之生活，彼此之间莫有半分丝毫之断隙。

sections.english: What more do you want? To live on? Or is it to continue sensation and impulse? To wax and then to wane? To make use of your voice, your mind? What in all this strikes you as good cause for regret? But if every one of these objects is contemptible, go on then to the final aim, which is to follow reason and god. But it is inconsistent with honouring these aims to be grieved by the loss of things contemptible.
sections.chinese: 你更有何求？继续存活？抑或仅是延续知觉与冲动？此身之发育渐兴，然后随之衰朽凋萎？运用你之声音、你之心智？在这一切之中，有哪一点足以令你觉得可惜堪为后悔之由？然若其每一对象都不值一哂，那便径赴那终极之目标吧，那就是：追随理性与神。然若因失去那些微不足道之物而悲切，便与尊崇此等目标水火难容。

sections.english: What a tiny part of the boundless abyss of time has been allotted to each of us — and this is soon vanished in eternity; what a tiny part of the universal substance and the universal soul; how tiny in the whole earth the mere clod on which you creep. Reflecting on all this, think nothing important other than active pursuit where your own nature leads and passive acceptance of what universal nature brings.
sections.chinese: 你我世人，所分得之时间何其微末——无几顷刻，转瞬即消逝于永恒之中；于宇宙实体之中、于宇宙灵魂之中所占之份何其区区渺渺；于整个大地之上，你匍匐其上的那小片泥土又何其纤芥。于此沉思之后，除却主动追随你自身本然所引之道，与默然接纳宇宙自然所带来的安排之外，勿以任何别事为重。

sections.english: How does your directing mind employ itself? This is the whole issue. All else, of your own choice or not, is just corpse and smoke.
sections.chinese: 你主导之心智，其当下运转如何？此即是全部之枢纽。一切其他之事，无论在你自择与否，仅是死尸一缕与过眼之云烟而已。

sections.english: The clearest call to think nothing of death is the fact that even those who regard pleasure as a good and pain as an evil have nevertheless thought nothing of death.
sections.chinese: 教人不必畏死之最明白之召示乃是：即便是那些以逸乐为善、以痛苦为恶的人，也不曾将死亡放在心上。

sections.english: For one whose only good is what comes in its own proper season, who is equally content with a greater or lesser opportunity to express true reason in his actions, to whom it makes no difference whether he looks on this world for a longer or a shorter time — for him even death has no terrors.
sections.chinese: 于那唯一以适时而来者为其善好、以行动中或大或小之机缘平等从容地体现真正之理性、且凝注此世之时日是长是短了无关碍的人而言——于他而言，即便是死亡也了无所畏。

sections.english: Mortal man, you have lived as a citizen in this great city. What matter if that life is five or fifty years? The laws of the city apply equally to all. So what is there to fear in your dismissal from the city? This is no tyrant or corrupt judge who dismisses you, but the very same nature that brought you in. It is like the officer who engaged a comic actor dismissing him from the stage. 'But I have not played my five acts, only three.' 'True, but in life three acts can be the whole play.' Completion is determined by that being who caused first your composition and now your dissolution. You have no part in either causation. Go then in peace: the god who lets you go is at peace with you.
sections.chinese: 有死之人啊，你曾在此伟大之城邦里以一公民之身分生活。这人生是五年，还是五十年，又有何分别？城邦之律法，普施一律，公允无遗。那么，你之被遣离此城邦，又有何可畏？遣你离去者并非暴君或贪腐之判官，而乃是那当初将你带引入来的同一自然。正如当初雇了那喜剧优伶之司事，最终遣他下台一般。「可是我尚未演完我这整五幕戏，我只行了三幕。」「或许如此，但人生之中三幕也够成一场整出的戏了。」完成此事的决裁，乃出于那当初首为造成你之合成、而如今又为你之消解的同一存在者。这两重因果的发生，你都没在其中占有一分促成之因由。那么，就平和而无牵怨地去吧：那放开你、让你离开之神，他对你也平和而无怨尤。
